number.why: The served observed-case Day-28 raw change-score estimate is supported: esketamine plus oral antidepressant −10.1 (SD 10.80, n=109) versus placebo plus oral antidepressant −8.1 (SD 10.26, n=106), giving a reconstructed MD of −2.0 MADRS points and SE 1.436378. These are evaluable participants within the FAS, not the entire FAS. The published MMRM estimate also rounds to −2.0 but has a different SE and 95% CI; that interval must not be attributed to the reconstructed raw MD.

entry.why: The population and comparison meet the question: adults with MDD and at least two adequate antidepressant failures before randomization, assigned double-blind to intranasal esketamine or matching placebo, each with a newly initiated oral antidepressant. MADRS change was assessed at Day 28. The screening history of as few as one previous failure does not contradict TRD eligibility: nonresponse to a different current antidepressant was additionally required before randomization.

quotes.span: The study population included adults aged 18–64 years, who met the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5) criteria for single-episode MDD or recurrent MDD without psychotic features, based on clinical assessment and confirmed by the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI).
TRD was defined as lack of clinically meaningful improvement after treatment with at least 2 different ADs at adequate dose and duration (≥6 weeks) in the current depressive episode.
Only patients with non-response to at least 2 AD treatments prior to randomization were eligible to participate in the study.

At the start of the 4-week screening/prospective observational phase, patients were required to have had documented nonresponse (≤25% improvement) to treatment with 1–5 oral ADs at adequate dose and duration based on the Massachusetts General Hospital – Antidepressant Treatment Response Questionnaire (MGH-ATRQ) for the current depressive episode and confirmed by documented records. In addition, patients were currently receiving a different oral AD (on the MGH-ATRQ), to which they had been adherent for at least the previous 2 weeks at or above the minimum therapeutic dose. Patients who were non-responders to their current oral AD(s) were eligible for randomization if all other entry criteria were met.

A computer-generated randomization schedule was used to randomly assign patients in a 1:1 ratio to receive double-blind treatment with either intranasal esketamine or matching placebo, each in combination with a newly initiated open-label oral AD.
The primary endpoint was change in MADRS total score (7-day recall) from baseline to Day 28 (end of double-blind treatment phase).

missed: No finding changes either verdict. The crucial qualification is that the published adjusted MMRM result and the reconstructed observed-case raw MD share the rounded point estimate but are distinct estimates with different uncertainty, as quoted above.
